name: Response must actually invoke the availability method somewhere: any isAvailable invocation present vs solution that never calls it
side_a: Award A1 whenever the response contains an actual invocation of the availability method with a String argument anywhere in the constructor — e.g., inside an if condition, a while condition, or a loop body (isAvailable(requestedName), isAvailable(nameToCheck), isAvailable(requestedName + suffix)). The point is for making the call, regardless of whether the surrounding loop/assignment logic is correct, off-by-one, infinite, or skips the no-suffix case.
side_b: Deduct A1 when the response contains no invocation of isAvailable at all — i.e., the constructor merely assigns the requested name (or otherwise sets username) without ever testing availability. Omitting the call entirely cannot earn the call point, no matter how syntactically clean the code is.

name: Availability is actually tested via isAvailable vs. name assigned unconditionally
side_a: No deduct if the constructor actually invokes the isAvailable helper on a candidate name (either in an if-test or a loop condition) before committing a value to username.
side_b: Deduct if the constructor never calls isAvailable at all and simply stores the requested name (or any name) directly into username.

name: An actual increment statement inside the loop body is required vs merely having a counter variable used in the loop (condition/concatenation) suffices
side_a: Give the point (no_deduct) when the answer contains an explicit statement that advances the counter (e.g. `i++`) placed inside the repeating body, so the counter value changes on each pass.
side_b: Deduct when no statement anywhere advances the counter — i.e. the counter is only declared and read (in the `while` condition or in string concatenation) but never incremented, or there is no counter/loop at all.

name: Tries the unmodified requestedName first (and assigns it when available) vs. never testing/using the bare name
side_a: no_deduct — the answer first calls isAvailable on the unmodified requestedName and assigns that exact string to username when it is available, only falling back to appended numbers otherwise.
side_b: deduct — the answer never tests the bare requestedName as a candidate: it either assigns it without any availability check, or it jumps straight to appending a number so the plain name can never be chosen.

name: Appended counter starts at 1 vs. starts at 0
side_a: no_deduct — the numeric suffix appended to requestedName begins at 1, matching the specified sequence (name1, name2, ...).
side_b: deduct — the numeric suffix begins at 0 (or any other value), so the first candidate tried is requestedName+"0", which is off by one from the required sequence.
